summary.text: Brett Wynkoop is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee challenging incumbent Jo Anne Simon for NY State Assembly District 52. A U.S. Merchant Marine Academy graduate and former Naval Reserve lieutenant who has worked in technology, run a charter sailboat business and taught computer science, he ran for this seat in 2022 and 2024 and for New York City Council District 39 in 2021 and 2025.

paragraphs.text: Wynkoop says he grew up in a military family, the son of a father who spent 30 years on Navy submarines and a mother who was a registered nurse, and attended 12 public schools across the country.

He graduated from the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy at Kings Point, served as a Naval Reserve officer reaching the rank of lieutenant, and built a career in technology specializing in Unix, networking and security, according to his campaign website.

In New York he says he ran a sailing school and charter boat business at the 79th Street Boat Basin and owned an IT firm, and that after COVID-era layoffs from healthcare site reliability work he returned to captaining charter sailboats and teaching computer science.
Wynkoop first appeared on the ballot as the Conservative Party candidate for New York City Council District 39 in 2021, finishing second with 7.8% of the vote behind Shahana Hanif.
He ran for Assembly District 52 in 2022 on the Republican and Conservative lines, receiving 7.9% of the vote against Jo Anne Simon, and again in 2024 on the Conservative line, receiving 5.8%.
In the November 4, 2025 general election he ran again for Council District 39 on the Conservative line and received 8.7% of the vote, and incumbent Hanif won.
Wynkoop is the Republican and Conservative Party nominee in the November 3, 2026 general election; both party primaries were canceled.
